cards.claim: UBA learning rate schedule achieves superior accuracy on CIFAR-100 ResNet34 at 25% training budget (75 epochs)
cards.conditions: CIFAR-100, ResNet34, 75 epochs (25% of standard 300 epoch training), standard training without TTA
cards.effect: 74.60% accuracy vs. 73.64% for best baseline (REX), a gain of 0.96 percentage points
cards.evidence: Experimental results table comparing six baseline schedules
cards.quote: Table 2: CIFAR100 ResNet34 at 75 (25%): UBA(ours) 74.60 ± 0.1508 vs REX 73.64 ± 0.5635

cards.claim: UBA schedule shows particular effectiveness at constrained iteration budgets (25% and 50% of full epochs)
cards.conditions: CIFAR-100 and ImageNet with ResNet architectures, multiple epoch budgets
cards.effect: UBA consistently outperforms at 25% and 50% budgets, demonstrating budget efficiency
cards.evidence: Comparative experimental evaluation across datasets and architectures
cards.quote: (ii) UBA outperforms baselines not only at 100% training budget but also at 25% and 50% iteration budgets, demonstrating its budget efficiency, i.e. effectiveness in computation-constrained scenarios.

cards.claim: Learning rate schedule design fundamentally impacts accuracy achievable under fixed iteration budgets, as evidenced by UBA's consistent superiority across diverse architectures and datasets
cards.conditions: Vision tasks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet) with ResNet18/34/50, multiple epoch budgets
cards.effect: UBA achieves measurable accuracy gains across small-scale (CIFAR) and large-scale (ImageNet) benchmarks relative to alternative schedules
cards.evidence: Comprehensive experimental comparison in Table 2 across all dataset and budget combinations
cards.quote: We find that: (i) UBA demonstrates the strongest performance across all training budgets, achieving superior results on both small-scale (CIFAR10/100 with ResNet18/34) and large-scale (ImageNet with ResNet50) benchmarks. This consistent improvement highlights the generalizability across model and dataset scales.
